plan: Pick up the extinguisher and drop it below the hanging ball as a temporary support.
Release the ball onto that support, keeping the spike screened while collecting the other chest.
Push the ball onto the side ledge before retrieving the extinguisher. Clear the fire and descend to the exit.
Lift the lower arrow into the middle row to open the start.
Approach the upper-left chest by releasing the left arrow in stages and letting the ball fall out of its approach.
Return around the top of the lower arrow, push it down into a different row, and collect the right chest before exiting.
Keep the cork in place while moving the marshmallow above it to screen the spike.
Move the freed cork right, keeping space to stand below it. Push it up into the hole.
Collect the isolated chest and return through the bottom passage to the stairs.
Shift the bottom marshmallow left, then step into and out of the lower arrow lane to release it.
Reach the left chest around the shifted marshmallow. Push the left-facing arrow upward twice to open the upper passage.
Leave the cell below the upper ball sideways so it falls behind you. Collect the top-right chest and return to the stairs.
Climb onto the chest beneath the ball. Wait once to let the upward plant build a support at the height of the open cross passage.
Leave the ball onto that support and collect the shears on the right. Push the supported ball sideways out of the shaft.
Cut down through the vine to the final chest and exit. Releasing the ball too early traps it between the shaft walls.
Push the right marshmallow up twice and use the right pocket to approach the upper chest.
Push the marshmallow back down from above; this also releases the arrow behind you.
Approach the left chest from above, letting its ball fall. Push that ball right in stages until you can descend into the stairs.
Release the upper arrow and its supported ball, then collect the bottom-right chest from the right passage.
Push the fallen ball left onto the central chest, then move the central marshmallow down to make an escape route.
Collect the chest under the ball and leave sideways. Approach the exit ball from below and step aside to let it fall, opening the stairs.
Raise the left marshmallow into the top row before collecting the top-left chest; it then stops the left arrow.
Release the right-facing arrow from the middle row and leave the top arrow lane safely.
Collect the lower chest, step left to release its ball, then push the ball right to reopen the return path to the exit.
First visit the cell beside the upper ball and retreat to release the two-ball cascade.
Lower the upper marshmallow one cell, release the upper arrow, and collect the left chest.
Return and lower the marshmallow again. From the right, push the lower ball left onto its neighbour, collect the bottom chest, then leave right and continue to the exit.
Move the cork beside the left hole without plugging it. It must block the ball’s leftward rolling clearance.
Release the upper ball so it rolls to the right of the lower ball, screening the spike while you collect the right chest.
Bring the cork back to the left shaft. Only now use it to plug the lower hole, collect the last chest, and reach the exit.
Leave the chest below the lower ball stack alone. Reach the upper chest, release its ball onto the ledge, then push that ball left onto the stack.
Collect the arrow-lane chest and leave upward. The completed stack diverts the arrow into the upper pocket instead of the exit approach.
Collect the base chest, drain the stack into the hole, and return through the one-way passage to the now-clear exit.
Descend twice to grow the vine exactly to row 6 (one-based), leaving the row above open.
Leave the vine column, approach the arrow from above, and push it down.
The vine catches the arrow beside its stem, directly between the chest and the spike.
Collect the chest and cross just above the vine to the stairs.
compact-still-life-v1.insight: A living brake turns an arrow into a spike shield, but one extra growth closes the exit crossing.

counterfactuals.explanation: An extra initial growth makes the vine reach the only exit crossing before Blobbo can leave its column; exhaustive search from this legal prefix finds no solution.

plan: Leave the cork supporting the ball while approaching the ball from the left.
Push the ball right into the still-open hole; the ball disappears without filling it.
Now plug the same hole with the cork.
Take the chest below the former support, then cross the bridge to the stairs.
compact-open-for-business-v1.insight: The future bridge must first serve as the ball’s disposal chute.

counterfactuals.explanation: Plugs the hole before disposing of the ball; exhaustive search exhausts 19 states without a win.

plan: Descend twice so the vine tip grows into the spike’s row.
Collect the chest and shears in the sheltered left chamber.
Cross through the lower stem while leaving the living tip intact.
Pass beneath the surviving screen to reach the stairs.
compact-pruning-time-v1.insight: Cut the stem below the crown: the disconnected upper vine remains a useful shield.

plan: Push the arrow up into the spike row; its rightward flight creates a horizontal shield.
Use that shield to reach and collect the chest above the marshmallow.
Return below the marshmallow and push it up twice into the upper lane.
Approach from its left and push it right beneath the exit, creating the vertical shield needed to enter the stairs.
compact-crosswinds-v1.insight: The arrow buys access to a second shield, and that shield must change lanes before the exit is safe.

counterfactuals.explanation: After this legal prefix, exhaustive continuation search finds no win (100 unique states; finite board has no growing plants or tools). Events: push:M.

plan: Leave the upper chest in place: it is holding the ball above the cork lane.
Push the cork all the way right to fill the hole.
Climb below the chest, collect it, and leave left so the ball drops behind you.
Return by the left loop; push the ball twice into the newly filled landing square and take the stairs.
compact-arrival-order-v1.insight: The hole must be filled before the tempting chest releases a ball into the only route available to its cork.

counterfactuals.explanation: Actual-engine continuation exhausts 36 states without a win.

plan: Pick up the axe and place it in the spike lane from below.
Cross the lane on the shielded side and walk above the marshmallow.
Push the marshmallow down between the spike and the axe.
Recover the axe, carve the tree, push the canoe out of the gate and collect the chest.
compact-on-loan-v1.insight: The axe must protect the crossing before it can cut anything; a shield installed from the far side lets you reclaim it.

plan: Collect the chest and approach the ball from the left.
Push the ball across the stone shelf and the cork, then off the far edge.
Lower the cork into the bottom room and move it right above the resting ball.
Push the ball aside to gain the square needed to raise the cork.
Raise the cork back to the exit lane and plug the hole.
compact-over-and-under-v1.insight: The cork first supports the ball; the ball then occupies the exact square you need to send the cork back upward.

counterfactuals.explanation: Raising the cork immediately traps it against the ceiling; exhaustive search exhausts 220 states.

plan: Send the lower ball right until the chest stops its fall.
Release the upper ball and push it into the same shaft, where it rolls around the waiting ball into the right lane.
Circle below and push that second ball left twice to form a support under the first ball’s eventual landing square.
Push the first ball left into the protected landing square, collect the chest beside it, then retreat upward before taking the exit.
compact-catch-and-release-v1.insight: The first ball catches and diverts the second, then the second returns to support the first while Blobbo briefly prevents a sideways roll.

counterfactuals.explanation: After this legal prefix, exhaustive continuation search finds no win (57 unique states; finite board has no growing plants or tools). Events: push:O, fall:O, fall:O.

plan: Park the cork above or below its starting square so the first chest can be collected.
Collect that chest and leave safely sideways; the ball follows the ramp into the still-open hole.
Retrieve the cork from its parking square, then push it right along the cleared chest row.
Get above it using the upper loop; push it down into the hole and collect the final chest.
compact-temporary-address-v1.insight: The cork must be parked reversibly while the hole still serves as the ball’s disposal chute.

plan: Grow the vine into the spike’s row.
Push the left arrow down so the vine catches it on its right side.
Collect the left chest and shears, then cut the vine tip while the arrow provides cover.
Step down into the stem: leaving the row releases the arrow only after you are safely below it.
Cut through the root and collect the lower chest before exiting.
compact-intervals-v1.insight: The vine catches the arrow, which then replaces the vine as a shield for exactly the one step needed to cut through.

counterfactuals.explanation: Pushing the arrow before the vine reaches its firing row leaves the arrow on the wrong side. Exhaustive search from this legal prefix found no winning continuation (22 states).

plan: Step right to let the ball fall onto the centre ledge, then push it left into the bottom pocket.
Push the cork upward twice to enter the upper loop.
Circle over it, reverse direction and push the same cork four squares down.
Collect the chest and escort the cork across the lower room, up the right side, and into the exit hole.
compact-passing-place-v1.insight: The cork must first travel away from the hole so you can cross it and reverse its direction.

counterfactuals.explanation: Pushing the cork one square too far north traps it against the top wall; exhaustive search confirms no win.

plan: Raise the arrow into the middle corridor and let it fly to the wall.
Circle beneath it and raise it again into the ball’s landing column.
Push the ball right off its upper shelf; it lands on the relocated arrow instead of falling too far.
Collect the chest and return to the exit, now screened from the spike by the ball.
compact-between-floors-v1.insight: An arrow moved twice becomes the shelf that catches a ball at exactly the height needed to protect the exit.

counterfactuals.explanation: After this legal prefix, exhaustive continuation search finds no win (73 unique states; finite board has no growing plants or tools). Events: push:>, arrow:>, arrow:>.

plan: Take the shears and cut the vine immediately left of the extinguisher.
Put the shears down where they can be recovered from the lower room.
Lift the extinguisher from under the ball, then leave sideways through the cut opening.
Extinguish the lower fire, exchange the extinguisher for the shears, and cut through to the stairs.
compact-make-room-to-leave-v1.insight: The extinguisher is a ball support: cut its escape route before picking it up, and leave the shears recoverable for the second gate.

counterfactuals.explanation: Picking up the extinguisher before cutting its side exit is exhaustively unsolvable.

plan: Lower the upper cork into the shared transfer row.
Move the lower cork down one square to free the pushing square beside the first.
Use the first cork to bridge the dividing hole.
Recover the parked cork upward, send it through the new bridge, and turn it upward into the final hole.
compact-close-quarters-v1.insight: The second cork must first vacate the exact square needed to deliver the first, then return to use the bridge it helped create.

counterfactuals.explanation: Actual-engine continuation exhausts 16 states without a win.

plan: Release the arrow in its original lane, then push it down so the chest stops its flight.
Collect the chest and step downward to release the arrow into the ball’s column.
Approach beneath the ball, step sideways to let it land on the arrow, then push the ball left onto the neighboring shelf.
Push the arrow downward out of the way, then push the ball left again so it falls between the spike and the stairs.
Return through the room to the protected exit.
compact-late-checkout-v1.insight: Collecting the chest is a timed release: the arrow must first reach the chest so it can become a landing shelf for the ball.

counterfactuals.explanation: After this legal prefix, exhaustive continuation search finds no win (145 unique states; finite board has no growing plants or tools). Events: fall:O.

plan: Use the extinguisher on the first fire before exchanging it for the shears.
Park the extinguisher immediately to the right of the shears, where it will stop the released arrow.
Take the shears, retreat below, then push the arrested arrow upward into its alcove.
Cut the vine in the exit corridor, return for the extinguisher and put out the last fire.
compact-temporary-custody-v1.insight: The extinguisher must serve as the arrow’s temporary brake between its two trips to the fires.

plan: Drop the axe into the spike lane and cross behind it.
Leave the upper chest in place until you have pushed the left arrow downward from above.
Collect that chest, then push the arrow down twice more to install a permanent spike shield.
Recover the axe, carve the tree and push its canoe up into the parking bay.
compact-reservations-v1.insight: The tempting chest is holding the arrow in its useful lane; only the relocated arrow can make the axe safe to reclaim.

counterfactuals.explanation: Taking the upper chest and retreating before lowering the arrow releases it into an irretrievable side cell; exhaustive search finds no win.

plan: Push the upper cork down to the bridge mouth.
Shift the lower cork right, then lift it above the transfer row; use the clear standing square to spend the first cork on the central hole.
Continue lifting the second cork into the top bay, shift it right, and lower it into the cleared bridge lane.
Send it across, lift it into the final hole’s row, then push it right to reach the chest and stairs.
compact-out-of-line-v1.insight: The lower cork cannot simply turn right at the crossing: its needed standing square is inaccessible, so it must go up through the top bay and return down the adjacent lane.

counterfactuals.explanation: Actual-engine continuation exhausts 10 states without a win.

plan: Raise the left cork into the connecting lane and push it right to the upper turning square.
Go below the lower cork and push it up into that same lane.
Raise the first cork out of the lane, then send the second left into the vacated chamber.
Circle below the second cork and reverse it, sending it right into the lane you just cleared.
Use the first cork at the upper hole and collect the chest; then lower the second cork to the exit hole.
compact-switchyard-v1.insight: The lower cork must visit the other cork’s starting chamber and reverse direction before it can serve its nearby exit.

counterfactuals.explanation: Overcommitting a cork toward the lower wall makes the room unsolvable; exhaustive search exhausts 1291 states.
